newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 17.48 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 17.48 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 123 basis points to 17.48 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 40 billion bolivars of 177- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 18.70 percent coupon for a price of 100.55 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 18.71 percent

The bank also sold 15 billion bolivars of 266-day notes with a 19.13 percent coupon at a price of 99.13 percent, and 15 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 19.58 percent coupon at an average price of 98.68 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 13 basis points to 20.48 percent for the 266-day bills, and 70 basis points to 21.19 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
